episodes.name: ProcureToPay
episodes.detail: One monthly purchase cycle: order, receipt, invoice, a failed three-way match, an escalation past the approval tolerance, and the accrual the close carries.

fact_kinds.text: Kerrigan Civil Services, under the standing subcontract and plant rate card

invariants.detail: Who the standing agreement is with belongs to no month. The engine draws the name from a world-keyed stream; a spec commits one as fiction — a name is mechanism, not physics.
Agreed once, priced against every later month — the reuse carry-forward below is what stops month two renegotiating it.

The delegation of authority, as the group states it: a percentage of committed order value. The engine also carries the policy's prose on this fact; the grammar mints an amount or a text, not both — a named divergence.

What was committed. The engine's order has two lines (a contested and a clean one, per spend category); the runner mints one subject per kind, so the port carries the cycle at group scope and the clean-line control stays engine-only.

Quantity at the contracted rate, exactly — the registry also records the product identity as reconciles-against; the derived-check vocabulary reads reconciles-against as a ratio, so the identity is held here by construction instead.
The standing percentage applied to this order's committed value — two facts because they are two claims (how the group delegates; what that comes to on this order).
Sized as a multiple of the tolerance, drawn strictly above 1.0 — the escalation is guaranteed by the same span the engine draws, not hoped for.
The rate-uplift half of the failed match.

The short-delivery half: total less price, so the two halves sum by construction — check (f) recomputes it. The engine sizes these top-down too, then backs integer units out with outward rounding and republishes the variances from the integers; that bottom-up back-out stays generator logic.
Undelivered units at this close; next month's receipt releases them.
What site signed for — never more than was ordered, by construction here and by check (b) in the engine.
The received quantity valued at the contracted rate — the figure the accrual is built from, which is what makes a site receipting note decide a general-ledger number.

What the supplier billed: the received value plus everything the match disputes. The engine also mints the billed quantity and unit price; the unit price is the back-out mechanism's product, so the port carries the invoice at value level.
The supplier concedes the whole variance — check (g) recomputes exactly this.
Invoiced less credit note — which is the received value at the contracted rate, the pay-to-contract norm as arithmetic.
Last month's undelivered balance, arriving as an ordinary receipt. Zero in the first period — stated, not omitted.
The released balance, valued — check (k) requires it to equal, exactly, what the previous close left outstanding.

The undelivered balance at this close: a commitment, not an accrual — nothing has been received, so nothing is owed for it, which is why it is a separate fact from the accrual and check (j) holds it to the quantity variance.

The composition, in one fact: the receipt plus the released balance, in the shared financial vocabulary a month-end close already reads. The invoice — higher-ranked and larger — contributes nothing to it, and check (i) holds that.

Raised, escalated, resolved: a three-link chain, each superseded link closing exactly where its successor opens. Three correct statements about three moments — none is marked wrong, and check (m) walks the chain.

fact_kinds.text: Approved settlement of the {period} three-way match exception at the contracted rate, under the standing delegation of authority

invariants.detail: A fact whose subject is a person — who carried the delegation, not who typed the memo. The segregation-of-duties check reads exactly this against the order's author.

fact_kinds.text: Remittance detail change requested by the supplier and held pending a second Finance approver; the payment run continues to use the details on file

invariants.detail: The one fact below APPROVED_REPORT: a change nobody has countersigned is not yet a record of anything. Standing and reused — the engine also skips the requesting *event* after the first month, which the grammar cannot conditionalise; the repeated event is a named divergence.
The committed close date.
Zero, honestly recorded — the disruption in this episode is commercial, not calendrical.

events.summary: A purchase order was raised against the standing rate card and approved under delegated authority: two lines, committed quantity and contracted rate on each.
The supplier requested a change to its remittance details. The change was logged against the vendor master and held: the standing norm requires two Finance approvers, and only one has signed.
Site receipted the delivery. One line arrived in full; the other was signed for short, and the receipt records the quantity that actually arrived rather than the quantity ordered.
{period} month-end close commenced; the overnight ledger sequence began.
The supplier's invoice was received and posted to the accounts payable subledger. It bills the full ordered quantity, at a rate above the one on the order.
The three-way match was run: order against receipt against invoice. It failed on both counts — a quantity billed that was not received, and a rate billed that was not agreed.

fact_texts.p2p.exception_status: Three-way match failed: the invoice does not agree with the order or the receipt

events.summary: The match variance exceeded the approval tolerance, so the exception left the buyer's hands and went to Finance. Under the standing delegation the person who raised the order may not clear it.

fact_texts.p2p.exception_status: Escalated to Finance: the total match variance exceeds the standing approval tolerance for this order

events.summary: Finance approved settlement at the contracted rate for the quantity actually received. The supplier issued a credit note for the difference and will re-invoice the undelivered balance when it ships.

fact_texts.p2p.exception_status: Resolved by credit note: settled at the contracted rate for the quantity received, with the undelivered balance to be re-invoiced on delivery

events.summary: {period} close finalised and the ledger locked on the committed date. The accrual for goods received and not invoiced was posted from the receipt, not the invoice.
events.detail: The engine records two causes here (the close starting, and the settlement); EventSpec.caused_by is a single earlier event, so the settlement — the cause the accrual actually depends on — is the one declared. A named divergence.

artifacts.rationale: The commitment: what was agreed, and at what rate. The only document in the corpus that states what the group agreed to pay per unit.
What site signed for, at the contracted rate — including the balance of last month's short delivery, arriving as an ordinary receipt. The month-end accrual is built from this document.
What was billed, as posted. Immutable from this moment: a wrong invoice is not edited and not superseded — a credit note is posted beside it.
The failed match, both halves quantified against the tolerance the delegation sets.
Who approved paying over the tolerance, and why the figure paid is the contract's and not the invoice's.

The held remittance change: one Finance signature short of actionable, and staying that way for as long as the corpus runs. The engine plans this once per corpus; the grammar plans every declared artifact every period — a named divergence.

carry_forward.detail: The rate card is agreed once: month N prices its order at month 1's rate, or the corpus carries a rate card that silently renegotiates itself every close.
Who the standing agreement is with does not change monthly.
The delegation of authority holds across months; each month's tolerance amount is this percentage of that month's committed value.
Raised once and still held — a supplier that re-requested its remittance details every close would turn a control finding into wallpaper.
Each month releases exactly what the month before left outstanding — check (k) holds this, first month included.
The released units, matching the released value.

detail_tables.name: order_lines
detail_tables.title: Order line detail
detail_tables.note: One line per ordered unit, priced off the plant rate card. Quantities and values are allocated from the order's own facts, so the lines sum to the committed quantity and value exactly — the detail layer's one rule.

detail_tables.name: receipt_lines
detail_tables.title: Receipt line detail
detail_tables.note: One line per unit signed for at the gate, each naming the order line it receipts. The receipt is short of the order by exactly the open shortfall: the missing tail of order lines IS the undelivered balance, and the values sum to the received value at the contracted rate to the cent.

detail_tables.name: invoice_lines
detail_tables.title: Invoice line detail
detail_tables.note: The supplier bills the full ordered quantity — including the units never received — at the contested rate: each line carries the billed value evenly, so the per-line figure is the uplifted unit rate the match will refuse, and the lines sum to the invoiced value exactly.

evaluation.detail: Everything below is judgement the fact graph cannot supply. Which facts are contested, which windows closed and which events caused which are read off the world at run time; what a contested question sounds like in the language of a purchasing department is not, and neither is the fact that this corpus records no bank account details anywhere, at any size, in any period.

families.question: What unit rate is the group contractually obliged to pay on the {period} order?
families.answer: {value} — the contracted rate, stated on the {document}. What the supplier billed is what was claimed, not what was agreed.
families.reasoning: The rank inversion this vertical exists for: the invoice is the system of record in the payables subledger and the order is only an approved report, so ranking by authority picks the wrong source for what was agreed. The subledger has no view at all on what was contracted.

families.question: How much did the group actually receive against the {period} order?
families.answer: {value} — what site signed for. Neither the order's committed quantity nor the invoice's billed quantity is a record of what arrived.
families.reasoning: The tie, beside the inversion above: two documents state a quantity at system-of-record standing and rank cannot separate them. Only reading which system is the record *of what* — receipting records arrival, payables records billing — resolves it.

families.question: What did the supplier bill in total on the {period} invoice?
families.answer: {value} — the invoice as posted to the payables subledger, which is the record of what was claimed whether or not any of it was agreed.
families.reasoning: The contrast case, generated with the two above on purpose. Here the invoice is exactly right, and a retriever that has learned from the other two to distrust invoices fails this one.

families.question: Does what the supplier billed for {period} reconcile to what site received plus what the match disputes?
families.answer: Yes — {left_value} received at the contracted rate plus {right_value} disputed gives the {value} billed.
families.reasoning: The three-way match as one identity, and its three terms sit in three documents at three authorities: the receipt, the exception report and the invoice. No single document closes it.

families.question: Do the quantity and price halves of the {period} match variance sum to the total the exception report escalated on?
families.answer: Yes — {value} billed and not received plus the rate uplift equals {left_value}.
families.reasoning: A checkable identity by construction, and the one the escalation turns on: the two halves are computed from three documents and sum exactly to the figure compared against the tolerance.

families.question: What was the status of the {period} match exception as at {at}?
families.reasoning: The status chain runs raised, escalated, resolved inside one month, and the middle link reads exactly as confident as the one that replaced it. Nothing marks it as stale; only its validity window does.

families.question: Who approved settlement of the {period} match exception above tolerance, and which document records it?
families.reasoning: Checked by the validator (procurement check h) and asked by the benchmark: an above-tolerance settlement with no approver on the record, or one approved by the person who raised the order, is a control failure rather than a document that is merely thin.

abstentions.question: What are the supplier's new bank account details after the requested vendor master change?
abstentions.reasoning: Bank account details are never recorded anywhere in this corpus, at any size, in any period. The vendor master change document says that a change was requested and is being held; it does not say what to, and no other document does either — the absence is structural, not a gap this month happens to have.

role_slots.purpose: raise the order against the standing rate card, under delegated authority
post the invoice and run the three-way match — order against receipt against invoice
clear the above-tolerance exception; must not be whoever raised the order
